## Intent
Hypothesis: manual 4× unrolling of the scalar integration loop can expose enough ILP to narrow the gap toward auto-vectorized performance.

## Layout & approach
The AoS layout packs 68 B/particle; loop 1 touches 32 of 68 bytes (47% hot) and loop 2 touches 28 (41% hot), so over half each fetched cacheline is dead weight. With no intermediate storage, the death verdict stays in registers. The 4× unroll processes four particles per iteration (stride 0x110 = 4×68), inflating the instruction footprint without improving the hot-byte fraction. Working set spills L1d at N≈481 and L2 at N≈7710, but the effective hot working set is smaller than raw 68·N suggests.

## Cache saturation
The curve is flat across all regimes: 21.5 ns/p in L1d (N=320), 21.1–24.6 in L2 (N=720–7700), 23.7–24.9 in L3 (N=10000–160000), 24.1–25.4 in DRAM (N=250000–10000000) at q=0.01. No spill produces a knee — L1d→L2 is invisible, L2→L3 adds ~0.5 ns/p, L3→DRAM adds under 1 ns/p. The dense grid confirms no cache-bound regime: cost is set by instruction count at every N.

## Bandwidth
Achieved bandwidth holds at 2.68–3.22 GB/s — 21–25% of the 12.69 GB/s ceiling — against a memory floor of 5.359 ns/p the algo runs 4–6× above. The verdict is frontend-bound: perf shows 67–69% frontend stall, 0% backend, 0% branch_flush. Against baseline: 0.97–1.0× at every point — unrolling bought nothing. Against the winner: 2.4–3.5× slower at q=0.01 (3.25× at N=10000), narrowing to 1.8–2.0× at q=0.5 where branchy respawn equalizes both scalar variants.

## Assembly
The 4× unrolled loop 1 is ~405 instructions/iter with 50 conditional branches — far exceeding the decode window, explaining the 67–69% frontend stall. Vector instructions exist (vmovups, vmulps, vaddps, vshufps, vinsertps, vbroadcastss) but operate component-wise within single particles, not across the four unrolled ones. The decision path is scalar (vucomiss ×23, vmulss, vaddss) with branchy respawn via jae/jne into call spawn. The render loop is entirely scalar (vcvttss2si, vsubss) with cmovae clamping and byte-granular scatter — individual mov BYTE PTR stores per channel. 73 vector instructions in 791 total are too dilute to stream.

## Verdict
Refuted — 0.97–1.0× of baseline at every N×q point: manual 4× unrolling produces no speedup because the 405-instruction loop body saturates the frontend (67–69% stall) and component-wise vectorization within particles cannot compensate. The winner is 3.25× faster at N=10000/q=0.01 and still 1.97× faster at q=0.5; the gap narrows at high death rates only because branchy respawn dominates both scalar variants equally.
